findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - close is rerun while the same pushed head's CI changes from pending to green.
The new `check_reads` includes requests from earlier iterations, while the before-and-after counts accept requests for any commit. After the first iteration queries the pushed head, a later invocation can query both endpoints for a different head and still satisfy these assertions. The fixture in `tests/test_close.py:175` returns the current check results regardless of the requested commit, so the test can pass while a retry makes the current head ready using another commit's CI. Each iteration needs to establish that its new reads target the pushed head.

The board test still chooses `calls[-1]` at `tests/test_machine_views.py:596` after filtering on a shared query fragment. Also, `test_18_close` still collects broad check-run and status calls and selects `[-2:]` at `tests/test_close.py:624-625`. An additional matching request can change which calls these tests inspect and fail them even when the intended check remains correct.
